notes.title: Major Update: Dust Raiders v1.1.1
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/50e15e75fb8debba2cb28084a2dab698435f03b3.png"][/img][/p][h1]Major Update: Dust Raiders v1.1.1[/h1][p]The desert roads will never be the same. Our latest major update brings a host of new features, balance changes, and fixes that expand your journey through the world of Dust Raiders.[/p][h2]New Features[/h2][list][*][p]Free Play after Story Completion - Finishing the main storyline is just the beginning. Continue your adventure freely without restrictions![/p][/*][*][p]Crew Bonuses from Cargo - Some crew members now provide benefits even when stationed in Cargo. Move them into vehicles for additional bonuses.[/p][/*][*][p]Workshop Randomization - Workshop inventories now refresh daily, and items you sell will appear in stock.[/p][/*][*][p]New Equipment Tier - A new tier of gear has been introduced, expanding upgrade paths and build variety.[/p][/*][*][p]Looted Module Upgrade Chance - Combat loot now has a small chance to appear at a higher tier.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Balance Adjustments[/h2][list][*][p]Adjusted the range of the Twin Launcher.[/p][/*][*][p]Rebalanced prices of certain crew members and modules.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Fixes[/h2][list][*][p]Unused vehicles in the Caravan panel are no longer incorrectly marked as destroyed.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]This is the biggest update to Dust Raiders since launch, and it is only the beginning of what we have planned. Keep your eyes open! Update #2 – with New Game Modes is on the way!!!

Thank you for your support and constant feedback.[/p][p]See you on the desert trails.[/p]

notes.title: Dust Raiders – Post-Launch Roadmap!
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/2a9d51511bf8fcc1b52bc185473f115cb0337992.png"][/img][/p][h1]Dust Raiders – Post-Launch Roadmap + 20% Discount[/h1][p]Hello Raiders![/p][p]We’re kicking things off with some great news — [b]Dust Raiders is now 20% off for a limited time![/b] If you’ve been waiting to jump into the wasteland or invite a friend along for the ride, now’s the perfect moment.[/p][p]And that’s not all. Your feedback since launch has been invaluable (reviews, mails, discord, everywhere!) and today we’d like to share our post-release roadmap for [i]Dust Raiders[/i]. This roadmap is designed to expand replayability, add more variety, and give players even more ways to experience life in the deadly wasteland.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🔹 Update #1 – We break the shackles - the game goes on! 
\[~ September 16][/h2][list][*][p][b]Free Play after Story Completion[/b] – Once you finish the main storyline, you’ll be able to continue your journey in Free Play mode without time restrictions.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Crew Bonuses from Cargo[/b] – Certain crew members will now provide bonuses even when stationed in Cargo, reducing the need for constant reshuffling. Additionally, some of them will offer extra combat bonuses when moved into vehicles.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Workshop Offers Randomization[/b] – To make scavenging more exciting, workshop inventories will gain a degree of randomization instead of always being fixed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Additional Tier for Equipment[/b] – We’re introducing a new tier of selected equipment, giving you more upgrade options and deeper build variety![/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🔹 Update #2 – New Game Modes 
\[~September 30][/h2][p]We’ll be adding three distinct game modes:[/p][list][*][p][b]Balanced Mode[/b] – The current default experience[/p][/*][*][p][b]Trade Focus Mode[/b] – Greater emphasis on trading, with lighter combat challenges[/p][/*][*][p][b]Combat Focus Mode[/b] – More intense battles, while trading plays a smaller role[/p][/*][/list][p]All modes will be available in both manual save and Iron Road (no manual saves) variants.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🔹 Update #3 – Events & Vehicles
\[~ Mid October][/h2][list][*][p][b]New Random Events[/b] – The current pool of events will be expanded with fresh scenarios to increase variety.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Enemy Vehicles for Players[/b] – Enemy vehicles will become purchasable and customizable, offering more caravan diversity.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🔹 Update #4 – Expanded Quest Content
\[~Late October][/h2][list][*][p][b]More Quest Types[/b] – Enclave missions will be expanded, adding more diversity to mid-game progression.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Endgame Mission Variety[/b] – Transporting colonists will be made more engaging.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🔹 Update #5 – Challenge Modes
\[~Oct/Nov][/h2][p]We’ll be adding special challenge modes with unique mechanics and constraints, designed to extend replayability and provide new goals for veteran players.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🔹 Update #6 – Official Soundtrack[/h2][p]The Dust Raiders OST will be released. Many of you have praised the game’s music, and we can’t wait to share it in full.[/p][hr][/hr][h1]The Road Ahead[/h1][p]We’ll continue shaping [i]Dust Raiders[/i] together with your feedback.[/p][p]Thank you for being part of this journey. The road is long, dusty, and dangerous, and we’re glad you’re traveling it with us.[/p][p]Stay safe out there, Raiders.[/p][p]The Dust Raiders Team[/p]

notes.title: Dust Raiders v1.0.6 Update – Enemy Stun Reduction
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/50e15e75fb8debba2cb28084a2dab698435f03b3.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello Raiders![/p][p]We’ve heard your feedback loud and clear - many of you mentioned that the amount of stun effects from enemies, especially in the later stages of the game, felt overwhelming and disrupted the gameplay experience.[/p][p]In response, the latest update 1.0.6 reduces the number of enemies equipped with the Oil Spiller ability, which was a major source of stuns.  In previous updates, we also shortened the duration of stuns - which should also have a positive impact on gameplay balance.

This change aims to make combat smoother and more enjoyable without compromising the challenge.[/p][p]We truly appreciate your ongoing support and detailed feedback. Keep it coming, and stay tuned for more improvements![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: 🛠 Dust Raiders v1.0.4 – Update & Vehicle System Rework
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/203abc64a6a0760f4aab920550418a22786d4fbb.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]🛠 Dust Raiders v1.0.4 – Update & Vehicle System Rework[/p][p]Hey Raiders!
Update [b]v1.0.4[/b] is here, bringing a major overhaul to how destroyed vehicles work, along with some gameplay improvements and important bug fixes. Here’s what’s new:[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🚗 Reworked Destroyed Vehicle Mechanics:[/h3][list][*][p]Destroyed vehicles are [b]no longer permanently lost[/b] – they now remain in your caravan as [i]broken[/i].[/p][/*][*][p]However, there's still a chance you’ll lose some equipment from them.[/p][/*][*][p]Broken vehicles [b]cannot participate in encounters[/b] and [b]don’t increase your cargo limit[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]You can [b]repair them at Service Stations[/b] or [b]sell them at Workshops[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Any lost cargo is now stored in the [b]caravan wreckage[/b], so it can still be recovered.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]⚙️ Gameplay Improvements:[/h3][list][*][p]Goods transferred from factories now go [b]directly to your Cargo[/b], instead of the enclave Warehouse.[/p][/*][*][p]There is now a chance to earn [b]fuel as a reward[/b] for winning encounters – every drop counts in the wasteland![/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]🐞 Bug Fixes:[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where [b]fog of war progress was lost[/b] after changing scenes without saving.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed several bugs that could [b]cause combat to get stuck[/b].[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]Thanks again for all your feedback and bug reports – your support helps us keep Dust Raiders moving forward!
Stay safe out there... and remember, even a wreck might ride again. 🚛💥[/p][p]– The [i]Dust Raiders[/i] Team[/p]

notes.title: Dust Raiders v1.0.3 Update
notes.notes: [h1]Dust Raiders v1.0.3 – Changelog[/h1][p][/p][p][b]🔧 Listening to your feedback, we’re introducing some gameplay changes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Jobs became the most profitable source of income in the previous version. That was never the intended design. Trading goods should be the main income, while Jobs are meant to be a supplement or a fallback option when you lose everything. With this patch, we’re restoring the balance from the Demo and Beta versions: Trading yields higher profits, fewer job offers, and lower rewards.[/p][/*][*][p]When you lose a crew member due to an event, the game now removes the least valuable crew member from Cargo first. If there is no crew in Cargo, the least valuable crew member from your vehicles is removed instead.[/p][/*][*][p]The chance of losing gear and crew from destroyed vehicles has been reduced from 30% to 20%. Still, if the entire caravan is destroyed, preserved items are stored in the wreck at the crash site. If only an escort vehicle is lost, the preserved items will be assigned to your Cargo.[/p][/*][*][p]Wanderer mode autosave now triggers only at safe points — when entering or leaving an enclave, or quitting the game. This ensures that if you haven’t created a manual save, you can still return to a relatively safe moment. Manual saving is still available at any time.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]🔧 Other Fixes and Changes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Added a Garage site to the Windmill enclave[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Hell Laser rotation speed for better tracking of fast targets[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue with invincible vehicles during combat[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the issue with vehicles not being destroyed by large obstacles[/p][/*][*][p]Improved some localization issues[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted volume for some sound effects[/p][/*][/list][p]We hope these changes bring a little more joy to your gameplay :)[/p]

notes.title: Dust Raiders Demo v0.7.9 is Live
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/cb03187b644d5d56656013b56929ad0b21d8abe4.png[/img]

We're excited to release Dust Raiders Demo v0.7.9, a significant update our small team has been diligently working on for the past two weeks. We've carefully reviewed and incorporated your valuable feedback, aiming to address as many reported issues and suggestions as possible. Please keep in mind that we're a very small team, and while we strive to improve the game consistently, your patience and understanding are greatly appreciated.

Check out the full changelog below, and as always, thank you for your ongoing support!

[h3]Dust Raiders v0.7.9 Changelog[/h3]

[b]Gameplay & Balancing[/b]
[list]
[*]Additional random Points of Interest now appear on the map.
[*]Jobs in enclaves no longer point to locations inaccessible to the player.
[*]Combat slow-motion now nearly stops time, is no longer time-limited, and can be toggled freely without holding down the space bar.
[*]The next wave of enemies in combat appears immediately after defeating all current enemies.
Increased Recon Scanner range.
[*]Jobs-related cargo is no longer lost when the caravan is destroyed.
[*]The Alcohol delivery to the Plenty enclave mechanism was reworked to give the player better control. [*]We also reduced the amount of alcohol required for delivery.
[*]Early-game combat encounters have become easier.
[*]Player escort vehicles now have increased Durability.
[*]Sniper-equipped enemies now attack the closest vehicle, making it easier to avoid player vehicle destruction.
[*]Pushing enemies into obstacles has become easier.
[*]Increased fuel tank capacity, compensated by adjusted fuel consumption and reduced refueling costs for better realism.
[*]Increased equipment selling price in the Workshop from 25% to 35% of the purchase price.
[*]Reduced the cost of bribing attacking gangs.
[/list]
[b]UI & UX Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*]Added the ability to preview active vehicle stats in the garage.
[*]Added cargo and warehouse icons to give a clearer indication of their purpose.
[*]Added a hint on how to skip the intro.
[*]Courier Job cargo is now clearly displayed on Job Boards.
[*]Item icons are now centered on the cursor during drag-and-drop for easier placement.
[*]Newly purchased vehicles automatically join your caravan (if a free slot is available).
[*]Now you can leave locations and enclaves using the ESC key.
[*]A bug-reporting button was added to the combat interface.
[*]Improved the description of damage dealt by the Shotgun.
[*]Valuable rumors can now be purchased at the Shelter enclave (previously free so often ignored 😄).
[*]Improved enemy targeting in tutorial combat.
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed animations for heavy vehicle damage.
[*]Fixed Oil Spiller functionality.
[*]Fixed issues causing the Rocket Launcher to deal no damage occasionally.
[*]Fixed Ramming action animations.
[*]Cargo Hold Extension modules tier 2 and 3 now function correctly.
[*]Resolved issues with selecting higher resolutions on some monitors.
[*]Fixed issues related to the Side Slam action.
[*]Fixed bugs occurring when rapidly spamming combat actions.
[*]Crew member fuel cost reduction effect now functions correctly.
[*]Burning debris sound near the Refinery now only plays when debris is visible.
[*]The first game event now displays the correct name.
[*]Numerous translation errors have been fixed.
[/list]

Enjoy your adventure in the wastelands!

notes.title: Dust Raiders - A UI Designed for Survival - Devlog #05
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/73ce92f32f58c0becc4d4a24a35e70cba5b60c18.png[/img]

In the harsh world of Dust Raiders, information is power, and a well-designed user interface (UI) can mean the difference between life and death. Today, we're excited to give you a sneak peek into the UI of Dust Raiders and how it enhances your gameplay experience.

[h3]Concept vs the current design[/h3]
The first version of the UI was created for the trailer when the game was in early development. As the project progressed, our needs evolved. However, this initial design helped establish the general mood, and the final icon design is a natural evolution of that style.

We've refined the icons, but more importantly, we've added clearer and more contextual information around your Caravan.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/1463e9ea37e3f0a64a7ba28d8da47f34796e9f72.png[/img]

In the heat of battle, every second counts. That's why we've designed our combat UI to be both informative and unobtrusive. It provides all the crucial information - health, ammunition, enemy positions - without cluttering your screen. The result is a fluid combat experience that lets you focus on the action while making tactical decisions on the fly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/fe12b53c449862d93eec12b4cd04c1d7c23c4bb8.png[/img]

The vehicle part now takes slightly more space to make sure you can see the attack icons, status, health and shield. We have also added red elements on the raider’s armor to make sure to more clearly distinguish them between enemies and foes.

[h3]Enclaves - the last prospering settlements[/h3]
Before driving into the unforgiving desert, you must carefully plan your route. This involves locating optimal enclaves to ensure you can meet demand with goods from nearby settlements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/5ae39743287d2b9c3f80304cb3c59e14f46989f4.png[/img]

Each enclave features unique artwork to help you identify its location. The same applies to Points of Interest (POIs) scattered across the map. Just keep in mind that the array of buildings and available services differs between enclaves.

[h3]Wasteland Trader[/h3]
In the world of Dust Raiders, resources are scarce, and trading is crucial for survival. Our focus is to make sure the dynamic supply and demand, resource availability, pricing and your cargo capacity are all quickly glanceable and adjustable at the one view.

On the left side you can see the current stock meter which is the key indicator regarding the needs of the enclave. It takes time to restock and information on the right will help you identify the source of resources and the dedicated supply chains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/ca0ab8728be37120f7055378470e5df69d79a447.png[/img]

[h3]Ruthless fleet[/h3]
Last but not least is the vehicle and weapon crew management. This crucial element ensures you're prepared for any encounters. You'll need to strategically assign your crew to maximize your chances of survival in the unforgiving wasteland.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/7c31175a012ac9ef83385f40f75fc4ed8fa187cd.png[/img]

Your caravan consists of the main vehicle, which has the most customizable slots, including special weapons and up to 2 crew members. The supporting cars have less slots and much more fragile. You can also see your maximum cargo capacity or a set of unused vehicles if you have managed to secure more for your fleet.

And that’s it for today’s devlog!
In the coming updates, we will delve deeper into the other gameplay elements of Dust Raiders. So, keep your engines running, and stay tuned for more exciting news about your favorite post-apocalyptic vehicular combat game. Remember, in Dust Raiders, it's not just about surviving - it's about thriving.
We'll see you in the wastelands.

notes.title: Dust Raiders - Narrative- Devlog #04
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/6c756d1b21ae9ff3a40920bbe6a2e77e895acf69.png[/img]

The world of Dust Raiders is filled with roaring engines, ruthless gangs, and desolation spanning deserts, swamps, and arid steppes. It’s a realm where, through trade and violence, you can seize power and dominate the perilous wastelands and key routes between enclaves.

Creating such a world from scratch is an immense task. Designing diverse map areas to each enclave, NPCs while making sure the world is believable and full of dozens of little storylines that player approaches through quests.

To help us craft a rich and intricate world, we’ve invited Marek Mydel, narrative designer and co-author of the critically acclaimed board game “Waste Knights: Second Edition”. We posed several questions to him about his inspirations, workflow, and past experiences.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/aea5017d378178f595eb56d50a04067554f1670a.png[/img]

[b]Hello, Marek! Could you tell us a bit about yourself? How did you become a board game designer?[/b]
I’ve been working in the industry for 20 years now, but it’s hard to say what makes you a designer. First I played any games that were available in the ‘90s in bleak Poland and then I was a guy who had a chance to work with great licenses either as a developer or translator. Hard to say when it happened. So, all in all, it’s more a matter of being in the right place at the right time rather than having a planned career as a designer.

[b]With Waste Knights, and now Dust Raiders, you’ve delved deeply into the post-apocalyptic theme. How do you blend expectations from these kinds of worlds with unique twists?[/b]
It’s always a bit of what I see in various games, movies and books and what I read on the news. Our world is already fu**ed up enough to give me inspiration. And then I fu** it up even more (for players’ sake, of course). Oh, and there are so many post-apo conventions in Poland and tons of great people who inspired me. Kudos to them all!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/c3a993c06820e4b3e35c5b4748b02e87c16725cf.png[/img]

[b]What are the differences between designing a board game and a video game?[/b]
One word – assets. It’s easy to write a passage in a choose-your-own-adventure book. It’s simple to create whole worlds like that.
But with a video game, I must limit myself to what the producers have in store. So, it’s a game of making the most of what they give you, which is a challenge by itself, but a nice one. Plus I quickly get to see what I imagined, while in a board game some things forever stay purely textual.

[b]You have experience translating ancient Japanese literature; what lessons from that work are useful today?[/b]
Don’t be a peasant in feudal Japan, ‘cause you might get cut. And then – appearances matter most. Samurai might not be your noble warriors, but they look like ones. Oh, and working 14 hours a day is a normal thing. Comes in handy when you’re handling a game project close to a deadline.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/3c552d2ff006a9194f11ef83096f32ea549b5a8a.png[/img]


[b]In Dust Raiders, we will continually fight and gain influence at the expense of different gangs. Could you describe one of the raider groups?[/b]
As I don’t want to spoil too much, so I’m going to tell you about the Skaters. One day after the Apocalypse they looted a hockey stadium and thought that wearing a mask with a bad-ass illustration sounds good. Some of them even tattoo their faces to make them look really fearsome!


What are your main sources of inspiration when designing the setting for enclaves in Dust Raiders?
This one is easy. I look at some place through my window or imagine one I don’t see and then think what will happen to it if no one delivers power and water to it. And when some bad guys come to claim what’s of any value there.


[b]What’s the secret to creating unique characters in a post-apocalyptic world?[/b]
I don’t think that such characters are far different from people living here and now. Post-apocalyptic world is simply one 20 years from now if we lack food and water. Imagine your neighbor in this situation – how would they react? Or you? And you have your unique someone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/5eece036be247d1dba3cfb5b6620e4e84b58d7b0.png[/img]

[b]Could you share with us some events that occurred before the plot of Dust Raiders?[/b]
There’s a whole plot twist we had to bury deep inside the game which basically underlines the whole idea behind the setting, but one thing which literally “sticks out” of it is “The Windmill”. Just get far enough in the game and you’ll see.


[b]What’s your favorite element of Dust Raiders so far?[/b]
I think it’s combat. As I work mostly with board games, all the action happening there is turn-based or dice-oriented. All in all, pretty static. But in Dust Raiders when you start a fight, better be prepared for some fast-paced decision making and exploding fun.

notes.title: Dust Raiders - Combat - Devlog #03
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/28e6b8ff2836134c6ea0372d238cc84db29686b3.png[/img]

Dust Raiders offers a unique blend of strategy and action, challenging you to make crucial decisions on the fly while also mastering the art of vehicular warfare. Each vehicle in your caravan is unique, boasting its strengths and weaknesses. Some machines are fast and agile, designed to dodge obstacles and pursue enemies. Others are heavy and robust, ready to ram and smash anything that stands in their way.

[b]Tactical combat with an active pause[/b]
The combat system in Dust Raiders works in real-time but still lets you have a lot of tactical depth. Using the active pause can help you prepare the plan for the whole combat, but if you are more willing to make decisions in split seconds, you still have the option to do so.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/347f000a35c0dd92a6e67d89446e3bddbdac3fea.gif[/img]

[b]Manage your fleet[/b]
During later stages of the game, you will be able to control not only your caravan vehicle but the whole fleet of supporting vehicles with its strengths and weaknesses. You can't move the caravan during the fight to let you focus on the perfect positioning of other vehicles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/30a5bfcb1eee7e7cac6ee7d9f3d5e735ca22b746.gif[/img]

[b]The joy of ramming[/b]
There's nothing like the thrill of ramming another vehicle in Dust Raiders. A visceral sense of impact, sending enemy vehicles flying in dramatic explosions of twisted metal and flaming debris. But it's not just about brute force. The game's tactical depth means you'll need to choose your moments to strike, using the environment to your advantage and striking when your enemy least expects it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/b9190e6dcbc3e0246c4d32e486066f7acbbb744c.gif[/img]

[b]Risk-and-reward [/b]
However, these adrenaline-fueled battles come with high stakes. In Dust Raiders, combat isn't just a risk to your life - but your resources, modules, and crew members. Each vehicle lost is a blow to your caravan's strength and a drain on your goods. It means that every battle is a calculated risk. Are the potential rewards worth it? Only you can make that call.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/f5298011dcc383c76e84b5dc0621b3fc02e5a46b.gif[/img]

In the end, the choice is yours. But whatever you choose, you can be sure that Dust Raiders' vehicular combat will deliver a thrilling, tactical experience that keeps you on the edge of your seat. So gear up, hit the gas, and prepare for the ride!

In the coming updates, we will delve deeper into the other gameplay elements of Dust Raiders. So, keep your engines running, and stay tuned for more exciting news about your favorite post-apocalyptic vehicular combat game. Remember, in Dust Raiders, it's not just about surviving - it's about thriving. 

We'll see you on the wastelands.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2397450/Dust_Raiders/

notes.title: Dust Raiders - Machinery - Devlog #02
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/9360c2897e0baeb908dfe5ec700ed04f4560604d.png[/img]

Turn on the engines! Without vehicles, people who managed to stay alive through the apocalypse most likely wouldn’t survive for too long. Thankfully, even despite the step back that humanity faced, oil extraction still takes place, and diesel machinery comes to the rescue.

But let’s face it, these recycled vehicles wouldn't win a beauty contest, but still might have their own appeal. Let’s take a look at a few of the enemy vehicle designs.

The Boar Charger, designed to ram and smash enemies, is heavy, compact, and ready to jump over even the highest dunes. The front of the car was reinforced with metal spikes and a battering ram, while the back had a powerful engine and a nitro booster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/fdddd3698ab569fca7fc7563a93d34bd35a65124.png[/img]

Ribcage Quad won’t provide the most security for raiders, but as a part of spreading terror, it is quite functional. Resembling a skeleton of a large animal. The wheels are spiked and can crush anything in their way. This vehicle is not very fast or agile, but it can intimidate and frighten anyone who sees it. It is a symbol of the raider's brutality and savagery.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/3be4e52c786aaf8d65962e2b1b60b2882ea7006a.png[/img]

Spiker is a vehicle that no one wants to touch. It is said that the raiders who drive it often display the corpses of their enemies on the roof, impaled by countless spikes. The intercooler is fused with a large-caliber, twin-barrel machine gun that unleashes destruction across the wasteland. 

Spiker is fast and agile, able to dodge obstacles and pursue its prey.
These are just a few concept designs of the enemy vehicles, but how will you actually survive all those raiders' machinery?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/8f94b86f18ce2fb13d398d2b8bdb7104831260a5.png[/img]

Well, we won’t talk about your Caravan and its modules in detail, but let’s leave today’s update with a sneak peek of an upgraded mobile HQ and center of wasteland operations. Your Caravan won’t be the fastest or most agile, but through upgrades and supported vehicles will over time get a chance to survive more intense fights.

The good news is that this won’t be a free-for-all fight, because there will also be a supporting vehicle, enhancing your tactical capabilities. You will keep full control of all vehicles, and you can also assign your crew members to different ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/5e7f9b1eefc7b3418de6609af2ff758ab411a07b.png[/img]

But we will dive deep into these topics with the next few updates.

Our ride will take some time, and we will dive deep into various gameplay elements, our development process, or more stuff coming to Dust Raiders. Remember to add Dust Raiders to your wishlist and follow us on Steam.

See you next month!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2397450/Dust_Raiders/

notes.title: Dust Raiders - The World - Devlog #01/2024
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/35cb13d34a57035a910f4293b923d81bce2c478a.png[/img]

From the borders of the Eternal Desert to contaminated marshes and abandoned Polis, the world of Dust Raiders is for the toughest. And even those considered reckless will only survive with proper armor thickness and well-oiled machinery. 

In this devlog, we will start a monthly series sharing our inspirations, gameplay features, and development updates for Dust Raiders. Buckle up, and let's start the engines!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/806f491c2295ce179a0d6b43eaf7b4a944af6719.png[/img]

[h2]The world has shrunk[/h2]
It's been a long time since humanity broke the Earth's balance. The climate changed so vastly we can't even pinpoint the exact location. The old countries' names and continents are no longer used, with new practical ones being used.

The world shrinks immensely for the majority of people who remain alive. Worrying about their safety, they settled in small enclaves, desperately looking for resources and jobs that helped them make a living. But none of them could survive independently - mines are only located next to some of them, some have a better climate to grow plants, etc. They need to trade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/582b8de53138af3fc90a4f0f0b6b688b99fb3d85.png[/img]


The desolate spread between them is harsh, overrun by raiders, gangs and self-acclaimed rulers waiting for goods to be taken by force. Achieving a good balance between safety and profit differentiates random traders from the most influential ones. And it will be your journey to ride along.

[h2]Recycling is all that's left[/h2]
People establishing enclaves need to work with whatever materials are at their disposal. Sheet metal is relatively cheap and easily adjustable, although it's not the best when the sun hits hard. Fortunately, clouds do appear in this world. 

Humanity took a considerable step back in technology. Fortunately, the knowledge of extracting oil was not lost, and the power of petrol and diesel engines helped to fight the dark and cold nights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/47a2578e051d5b5e2fc5e226b925b27a44cc89da.png[/img]

Post-apocalyptic visions of small American villages inspire the design of the enclaves. The people there use whatever materials they can find to build their homes and defences, such as sheet metal, wood, concrete, and scrap. They also rely on oil and diesel engines to power their machines and vehicles, as they need to gain knowledge of more advanced technologies.

You might ask, why didn't people move on from such a harsh location to live in? Well, apart from the oil availability, they also can't. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44423194/df6d42642e790cde761703bf5e76f591726ced3c.png[/img]

It is surrounded by Eternal Dunes from one side, contaminated water from the other and huge mountains with collapsed tunnels. Stuck, trying to find a habitable place across the desert, nearby marshes and dunes. But also a perfect trade opportunity to rule the local economy in this new reality.

[h2]Stay tuned for more![/h2]
Our ride will take some time, and we will dive deep into various gameplay elements, our development process, or more stuff coming to Dust Raiders. Remember to add Dust Raiders to your wishlist and follow us on Steam.

See you next month!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2397450/Dust_Raiders/
